search.purpose: Search Notion pages and databases by free-form query string and return ranked smart-id results.
when_to_use: User asks to find a page or database by title without knowing the UUID
Disambiguating between similarly-named pages across the workspace
limitations: Search index lags upstream by a few seconds for newly-created pages
Returns only pages and databases the integration has been granted access to
search.parameter_overview: Required: query (free-form string matched against page titles and database titles). Returns: ranked smart-id array.

fetch.purpose: Fetch a single Notion page or database by smart-id and return its full representation.
when_to_use: Smart-id already known from a prior search() or list_objects() call
Need full property values not surfaced in list views
limitations: Single-object fetch only; for batch reads use list_objects()
Returns 404 if smart-id refers to a trashed or revoked-access object
fetch.parameter_overview: Required: id (smart-id of format notion-api:{type}:{collection}:{identifier}). Returns: full upstream object.

list_collections.purpose: List the available Notion collections (Page, Database) for discovery.
when_to_use: Discovering what types of data this server exposes before issuing list_objects() calls
Building a collection picker in a UI
limitations: Returns only collection metadata, not the objects themselves
Counts are upstream-best-effort and may exclude restricted-access pages
list_collections.parameter_overview: No required parameters. Returns: array of collection descriptors with name and approximate object count.

list_objects.purpose: List Notion objects in a given collection (database query) with cursor-based pagination.
when_to_use: Walking all rows of a Notion database
Building a paginated table view over a database
limitations: Only Database collections support list_objects (use search for top-level pages)
Default page size is 25, max 100 per call
list_objects.parameter_overview: Required: collection (database smart-id). Optional: limit, cursor. Returns: paged smart-id array of database rows.

upsert.purpose: Create a new Notion page (in a database or as a child) or update an existing page's properties.
when_to_use: Adding a new row to a Notion database
Updating a page's status, tags, or other property values by smart-id
when_not_to_use: Archiving a page — use delete() to soft-delete via archived flag
Editing block content (paragraphs/headings); this server only manages page-level properties
limitations: data must conform to the parent database's property schema; mismatches return validation errors
Partial property updates merge; pass full nested objects to replace them
upsert.parameter_overview: Required: data (page payload with parent + properties). Optional: id (presence triggers update path). Returns: created or updated page.

delete.purpose: Soft-delete (archive) a Notion page by setting its archived flag via PATCH.
when_to_use: Archiving a page that is no longer needed but should remain recoverable
Bulk-cleaning stale rows from a Notion database
limitations: Notion does not support hard delete via API; archive is the only deletion path
Archived pages remain in trash and count against workspace storage
delete.parameter_overview: Required: id (page smart-id). Returns: archived page object.
